question: Should this PR receive a monitored real-behavior-proof override, or remain draft until staging or a naturally occurring failed shard provides after-fix evidence?
rationale: Artificially inducing this control-plane failure would create unnecessary load and violate the stated operational guardrails, while automated tests cannot prove the deployed workflow, queue service, and deferred router interaction end to end.

options.title: Approve monitored canary override
options.body: Allow the PR to proceed with the first naturally occurring failed shard as the canary, requiring redacted queue/run evidence and immediate rollback if any documented invariant fails.

options.title: Hold for observed proof
options.body: Keep the PR in draft until staging, shadow execution, or a naturally occurring pre-merge path supplies after-fix workflow and queue evidence.

recommendation.title: Approve monitored canary override
recommendation.body: Allow the PR to proceed with the first naturally occurring failed shard as the canary, requiring redacted queue/run evidence and immediate rollback if any documented invariant fails.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining choice concerns production workflow proof sufficiency and rollback ownership rather than implementation mechanics.
